words.definition_en: to identify an illness by examining someone
example_sentences: The doctor diagnosed him with a mild infection.

words.definition_en: to officially recommend a medicine or treatment
example_sentences: The doctor prescribed antibiotics for the infection.

words.definition_en: a written instruction from a doctor for medicine
example_sentences: You need a prescription to buy this medicine.

words.definition_en: collocation: to arrange a specific time to see a doctor or specialist
example_sentences: I need to make an appointment with my GP.

words.definition_en: general practitioner — a doctor who treats general medical conditions
example_sentences: You should see your GP before it gets worse.

words.definition_en: a doctor who focuses on one area of medicine
example_sentences: She was referred to a specialist for further tests.

words.definition_en: to send a patient to another doctor for specialist treatment
example_sentences: My doctor referred me to a cardiologist.

words.definition_en: to become healthy again after an illness
example_sentences: It took him a month to recover from surgery.

words.definition_en: a return of illness after a period of improvement
example_sentences: He suffered a relapse two weeks after leaving hospital.

words.definition_en: (of an illness) sudden and severe, but usually short
example_sentences: He was admitted for acute appendicitis.

words.definition_en: collocation: an illness or health problem, often ongoing
example_sentences: He has an underlying medical condition.

words.definition_en: the amount of a medicine to be taken
example_sentences: Never exceed the recommended dosage.

words.definition_en: (of medicine) able to be bought without a prescription
example_sentences: This painkiller is available over-the-counter.

words.definition_en: to formally accept a patient into hospital care
example_sentences: She was admitted to hospital overnight for observation.

words.definition_en: to officially allow a patient to leave hospital care
example_sentences: He was discharged after three days.

words.translation_pt: ser operado, submeter-se a uma operação
words.definition_en: collocation: to have a surgical procedure performed
example_sentences: He underwent an operation last month.

words.definition_en: a drug used to prevent pain during surgery
example_sentences: She was given a local anaesthetic before the procedure.

words.definition_en: a condition causing a bad reaction to certain substances
example_sentences: He has a severe allergy to peanuts.

words.definition_en: collocation: the body's response to an allergen
example_sentences: She had an allergic reaction to the medication.

words.definition_en: swelling and redness caused by injury or infection
example_sentences: The cream reduces inflammation around the joint.

words.definition_en: (of a disease) able to spread by contact
example_sentences: Chickenpox is highly contagious.

words.definition_en: a sudden increase in cases of a disease
example_sentences: There was an outbreak of flu at the school.

words.definition_en: a widespread occurrence of a disease in a community
example_sentences: The city declared a health epidemic.

words.definition_en: a person's emotional and psychological well-being
example_sentences: The company now offers mental health support for staff.

words.definition_en: a feeling of worry or unease, often about the future
example_sentences: He struggles with anxiety before exams.

words.definition_en: a mental health condition causing persistent sadness
example_sentences: She was diagnosed with depression last year.

words.definition_en: collocation: experiencing mental or emotional pressure
example_sentences: He's been under a lot of stress at work lately.

words.definition_en: collocation: a diet containing the right amounts of nutrients
example_sentences: A balanced diet helps prevent many illnesses.

words.definition_en: containing substances the body needs to stay healthy
example_sentences: Try to eat more nutritious meals.

words.definition_en: a lack of something needed, especially a vitamin or mineral
example_sentences: He was diagnosed with a vitamin D deficiency.

words.definition_en: the physical or mental strength to sustain long effort
example_sentences: Marathon runners need great stamina.

words.definition_en: treatment of injuries through physical exercises and massage
example_sentences: She's having physiotherapy for her shoulder.

words.definition_en: the process of helping someone recover normal function after illness or injury
example_sentences: The rehabilitation programme lasted three months.

words.definition_en: collocation: an illness that cannot be cured and will lead to death
example_sentences: He was diagnosed with a terminal illness last year.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to prevent something harmful from affecting you
example_sentences: Vitamin C is said to help ward off colds.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to become ill with a minor illness
example_sentences: I think I'm coming down with something.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: to survive a serious illness or difficult situation
example_sentences: The doctors were confident she would pull through.

words.definition_en: idiom: tired and lacking energy, often before getting ill
example_sentences: You look run down — you should get some rest.

words.definition_en: idiom: recovering from an illness or injury
example_sentences: He's still weak, but he's on the mend.

words.definition_en: idiom: feeling slightly unwell
example_sentences: I'm feeling a bit under the weather today.

words.definition_en: idiom: an official statement that someone is healthy
example_sentences: The doctor gave him a clean bill of health after the check-up.

words.definition_en: idiom: gradual damage from normal use over time
example_sentences: The joint pain is just normal wear and tear from age.

words.definition_en: idiom: to have a harmful effect on someone or something over time
example_sentences: The long hours took a toll on his health.

words.definition_en: phrasal verb: (of a condition) to suddenly become worse
example_sentences: Her arthritis tends to flare up in cold weather.

words.definition_en: unable to get out of bed because of illness or old age
example_sentences: He was bedridden for weeks after the accident.

words.definition_en: a minor illness
example_sentences: She suffers from a number of minor ailments.

words.definition_en: a continuous, dull pain
example_sentences: I have a slight ache in my back.

words.definition_en: feeling like you might vomit
example_sentences: The medication can make you feel nauseous.

words.definition_en: to lose consciousness briefly
example_sentences: She fainted from the heat.

words.definition_en: collocation: to have a wound closed with thread by a doctor
example_sentences: He needed five stitches after the cut.

words.definition_en: (of an injury) to become healthy again
example_sentences: The wound healed quickly.

words.definition_en: an outbreak of a disease affecting a very wide area or the whole world
example_sentences: The pandemic changed the way many people work.
